arguments.content:
with results as (
  select statusId as status_id,
          raceId as race_id,
          driverId as driver_id,
          constructorId as constructor_id,
          resultId as result_id,
          grid,
          positionOrder as position_order,
          points,
          laps,
          fastestLapTime as fastest_lap_time,
          fastestLapSpeed as fastest_lap_speed,
          time as lap_time,
          milliseconds as lap_milliseconds,
          number as lap_number,
          fastestLap as fastest_lap,
          position,
          positionText as position_text,
          rank

    from {{ ref('src_results') }}
),

status_descriptions as (
  select statusId as status_id,
         status as status_desc
    from {{ ref('src_status') }}
),

position_descriptions as (
  select *
    from {{ ref('src_position_descriptions') }}
),

final as (
  select r.status_id,
         r.race_id,
         r.driver_id,
         r.constructor_id,
         r.result_id,
         r.grid,
         r.position_order,
         r.points,
         r.laps,
         r.fastest_lap_time,
         r.fastest_lap_speed,
         r.lap_time,
         r.lap_milliseconds,
         r.lap_number,
         r.fastest_lap,
         r.position,
         r.rank,
         s.status_desc,
         p.position_desc
    from results as r
    left join position_descriptions as p
  using (position_text)
    join status_descriptions as s
  using (status_id)
)

select *
  from final

text: FIXED: The staging results model dropped about 15,700 of 26,599 rows because `stg_f1_dataset__results` joined to `src_position_descriptions` with an inner join. That lookup only contains the six non-numeric codes (D, E, F, N, R, W), so every ordinary numbered finish had no match and was filtered out. I changed that join to a left join in `models/staging/f1_dataset/stg_f1_dataset__results.sql`, so all results are kept and `position_desc` is null for normal finishes. I rebuilt `stg_f1_dataset__results+` and it passed; the staging table now has 26,599 rows, one per result_id, matching the raw source. The `position_desc` column is populated only for the 10,930 rows with a code, which is expected given the lookup's contents.
